perspective:
**From Angela Hwang’s accessible perspective:**

I know I am Angela Hwang, a hairdresser, and that Kevin and I have been close friends since high school. I know Kevin works as a construction worker.

- I invited Kevin to coffee because I was worried he seemed unhappy with his job.
- I heard Kevin say he had been “alright,” just the usual grind, but then that he was unhappy, stuck, unfulfilled, and just going through the motions.
- I asked if a different job or career path might make him happier. Kevin said he had thought about it but did not know where to start and felt overwhelmed. I offered to figure out options together; he agreed and thanked me.
- I found job openings and a career counseling service, told Kevin about them, and asked if he had thought more. Kevin said he was interested in something more creative, maybe design or architecture. I encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would and thanked me.
- I believed Kevin was hesitant, felt frustrated and worried, and arranged a meeting with a career coach. I told Kevin I believed in him. Kevin said he appreciated it but was not sure he was ready. I said the coach could help him make a plan and gain confidence. Kevin agreed to give it a shot and thanked me.
- I checked in about the career coach. Kevin told me the coach had been helpful, he had started online courses in design, and he felt more confident about the change. I said I was proud and offered more help. Kevin said knowing I was there was enough and he would tell me if he needed anything.
- I organized a small celebration party for Kevin’s new career and told him. Kevin thanked me and said it meant a lot. I said he had worked hard and deserved it. Kevin said he could not have done it without me. I said he did the hard work and suggested enjoying the party.
- My own feelings across this included worry, hope, frustration, pride, relief, happiness, and satisfaction.

I do not have access to Kevin’s private thoughts or feelings except what he told me or showed me directly.
